title: "The loop"
description: "From a large plan to a roadmap, and from a task to reviewed commits."
sidebar:
  order: 1
---

For work larger than one task run, `forgecycle roadmap decompose <plan.md>` uses the selected
policy's `decompose` candidates in read-only mode to assess the plan and produce a
reviewable `roadmap.md`, a machine-readable `roadmap.json` manifest (task order,
files, prerequisites, and decisions document), a `decisions.md` of the decisions
a human must make, a copy of the source plan, and dependency-ordered task
files under `tasks/`. The Decomposer investigates relevant code, tests,
integration points, and constraints so each task contains repository-grounded
technical context and component-level change guidance. Use `--output DIR` to
choose another new directory inside the repository. Review the roadmap before
running the task files. The decomposition
stage does not produce the authoritative file-level implementation plan,
implement tasks, or declare them complete; in each task run, Planner
re-investigates the selected base and plans, and Reviewer keeps completion
authority.

`forgecycle roadmap run <dir>` then executes the reviewed roadmap with no
operator between tasks. Each task runs as an ordinary task run, with its own
state, handoffs, branch, worktree, and approval policy, strictly in
`roadmap.json` order and on a base that already contains every earlier task's
accepted work. After Reviewer's `done` verdict, the roadmap run fast-forwards
its own branch, `forgecycle/roadmap/<roadmap-run-id>`, to that task run's head.
It stops when a task run stops: recover the task run with `task` commands,
then continue with `forgecycle roadmap resume <roadmap-run-id>`. It never
answers a stop, approves a gate, skips a task by itself, or merges into your
branch. When the last task is done you review and merge one branch:

```bash
git merge --ff-only forgecycle/roadmap/<roadmap-run-id>
```

The approval policy decides how unattended a roadmap run is: `autonomous`
pauses only at stops, `custom` with `approval.checkpoints: ["final"]` pauses
once per task before it finishes, and `plan-and-final` twice per task. See
[Configuration](/documentation/guides/configuration/#approval-configuration). To run one
task at a time instead, use `forgecycle task run` on a base that already
contains the task's prerequisites.

```text
large plan ──► Decomposer assesses + decomposes
                         │
                         ▼
     roadmap.md + roadmap.json + decisions.md + task files
                         │ review, answer decisions (+ roadmap questions)
                         ▼
     roadmap run: for each task in order, a task run on
     the integration head; a done head fast-forwards
     forgecycle/roadmap/<roadmap-run-id> ──► you merge it
                         │ one task run
                         ▼
standalone task ───────► task.md
                         │
                         ▼
                   task snapshot
                         │
                         ▼
                   Planner plan ──► optional approval
                         │
                         ▼
                   Builder implementation + exactly one commit
                         │
                         ▼
                   Reviewer cumulative and latest-turn review
                         │
                         ├── changes requested ──► Builder
                         ├── needs human / blocked
                         └── done ──► optional final approval ──► result.md
```

Reviewer is the only completion authority. A successful review requires every
acceptance criterion to be satisfied, every finding to be closed, required tests
to pass independently, valid Builder commit history, and a clean worktree.

Models are not asked to echo values ForgeCycle already knows. Before
validating a handoff, ForgeCycle strips recognizable preambles, repairs glued
or missing front-matter delimiters, and fills omitted run IDs, turns, Git
revisions, and required-test commands. Wrong values are still rejected,
through a single in-turn repair. Each turn gets an `EVIDENCE_DIR` for logs and
probes. If a provider reports an exhausted usage quota, the candidate is put
on a cooldown and skipped until the provider resets.

## Decide everything up front

A roadmap run is meant to run unattended, so every human decision is asked
before it starts instead of stopping a task halfway through. `decisions.md`
holds one section per decision, written for someone who has not just read the
code or the plan:

```markdown
## Q02: Should the health endpoint require login?

**Context.** FC01 adds GET /healthz, which reports the service version. Today
every endpoint except /login requires a session.

**What depends on it.** A public endpoint shows anyone which version runs; one
that requires login needs credentials in the load balancer's health checks.

**Affects:** FC01

**Options**

- **Public**: works with any load balancer as is; exposes the version number.
- **Login required**: hides the version; health checks need a service account.

**Recommended: Public.** The version is already shown on the login page.

Unclear:

Answer:
```

The Decomposer must give every question this context, explain the terms they
use, give each option its consequences, and justify the recommendation, in
plain language with unambiguous dates (2026-10-30) and units (30 s, 512 MiB)
while quoting the plan and code exactly (`prompts/writing_questions.md`); a question missing a part is rejected. If a
decision is still unclear to you, write what you do not understand after its
`Unclear:` line, or type `?` and your question when `roadmap run` asks it, and
run `forgecycle roadmap questions <dir>`: the Decomposer, read-only, rewrites
that decision to answer what you asked, quoting your question, and looks for
decisions each task's Planner or Reviewer would still stop for, given the
answers so far.
You can add your own decisions as `## Qnn: title` sections with an answer.

`roadmap run` refuses to start while a decision is unanswered or unclear (exit
65, listing them); on a terminal it asks each unanswered one instead, and
`--accept-defaults` takes every recommended answer, never for a decision
marked unclear. The answers are snapshotted into the roadmap run and
given to every task run's Planner, Builder, and Reviewer as
`ROADMAP_DECISIONS`: binding human direction that they must not ask about
again. If a task still stops with `needs_human`, Planner or Reviewer writes
its questions in the same form, and the answer you give with `task resume --feedback` is
appended to the roadmap run's decisions too, so later tasks do not ask it
again.
